powergrid.gui.strut.slots.six: six runs, up to 2", in a panel's six positions
A 3 px rail on any face, with clamp slots along it marked by straps. Start a run at a knockout, then click the strut where it should clip; it goes there in straight legs and stays one piece over the next strut. With no run pending, a click marks the strut as the run's start, and the next click lays the run from it across the rail, for racks laid ahead of their panel. Sneak-click with an empty hand to choose the slots: six 2" that line up with a panel or a trough, four 3", two 4", or eight small ones. Click it with another strut to stack a second rail eight pixels out for a second row of runs; again to leave only the raised rail, again for a single. A strut placed on the outer face of a stacked strut carries on a tier further out, tied to it with a post. A wrench turns a strut the other way across its mount.

item.powergrid_modernized.conduit_bender: Bends and cuts laid conduit. Tap a leg to grab it at that point. Then tap a block face where it should go, and the leg slides there, resting on that face, the legs beside it following; or tap a point on another leg of the same run, and the tube runs straight between the two points in place of the corners. With a leg grabbed, the scroll wheel sets how far off the face it lands, a pixel a notch. Tap the grabbed leg again, or sneak-use in the air, to let go. Tap a diagonal to grab it, then tap a point on a leg to move its nearer end there. Sneak-click a diagonal to take it out; sneak-click any other leg to cut the run in two there, the wires in it coming out. The wire cutters take a piece away.

item.powergrid_modernized.fire_alarm_pan: The fire alarm control panel. Feed it 120 V through a knockout, splice smoke detectors to its initiating loop and horn strobes to its notification loop, and it watches the loops: a detector in alarm sets it off, the horns sound and the strobes flash, and it puts out a redstone signal. The left button silences the horns, the right resets once every detector is quiet. A loop with nothing on it is trouble. Three Form C dry contacts, Alarm, Trouble and Silenced, each a COM, an NO that closes on the condition and a supervised NC that is closed only while the panel is powered and clear, switch whatever is spliced through them: a contactor coil, a controls cabinet input. A monitor module in a gang box brings a flow switch or any other dry contact onto the loop; an annunciator, three gangs wide, repeats the lights, the display and the buttons anywhere on the loop. A Cat6 cable from the jack on its side to a controls cabinet's network puts it in the PLC: read FA, FA.TROUBLE, FA.SILENCED, FA.POWER, FA.DRILL, FA.3 for the device at address 3 and FA.Z2 for zone 2; write FA.SILENCE, FA.RESET and FA.DRILL. Click the display to open the panel's screen: the devices, their zones, and the buttons.

powergrid_modernized.ponder.conduit.head: Conduit
powergrid_modernized.ponder.conduit.text: Conduit boxes on a wall. Every edge carries knockouts, flat marks in the colour of the biggest trade size they take; the hubs light up while conduit is in hand

Click a hub, click the surfaces the run should follow, and finish on another hub. A run leaves each knockout square, in a short stub, before it goes anywhere, and the preview shows the route it will take

Right-click a closed run with building wire to pull a conductor through it. A run takes as many as its trade size allows, filled by the book, and the wires land on the boxes' hidden terminals for splicing

The Conduit Bender slides the leg under the crosshair sideways, one step a click, away from the face you click. The legs beside it follow and corners come and go, so offsets, kicks and saddles take a few clicks
Tap a leg with the bender to grab it and tap a face to move it there; sneak-click a leg to cut the run in two, so a mistake costs one piece
powergrid_modernized.ponder.fire_alarm.t: The fire alarm panel. Feed it 120 V through a knockout; it keeps 24 V on two loops of pulled wire, an initiating loop for detectors and a notification loop for horn strobes, spliced in its editor like any device

Smoke and heat detectors and pull stations are covers for the conduit box and devices for the gang box, on the initiating loop. In alarm each closes a resistor across the loop, and the panel sees the current
Horn strobes sit on the notification loop, as box covers or gang devices. The loop idles at two volts, enough for the panel to see them and not enough to wake them

Fire within four blocks of a smoke detector trips it. The panel goes to Alarm, drives the notification loop to 24 V, the horns sound the three-pulse pattern, the strobes flash, and the panel puts out a redstone signal
The left button silences the horns and leaves the strobes going. Put the fire out, and the right button resets the panel; it refuses while any detector or pull station is still in alarm
powergrid_modernized.ponder.breaker_pane: A breaker panel takes the service on its lugs and splits it into branch circuits, each behind its own breaker
The main breaker goes in the space at the top. Its poles match the panel: two on a split-phase panel, three on a three-phase one
Branch breakers click into the spaces below. The two spaces of a row share a leg and the rows alternate legs, so a 2-pole breaker across two rows gets both
Click a breaker to flip it. The load on that branch, here a light in a conduit box, comes on. A wrench scrolls the trip rating; it trips on its curve and goggles show its heat
The lugs take the service: a feed of the right size through a knockout in conduit, or hanging wire straight onto them
A panel cover closes the front. Sneak-click it to swing the door open and shut; the breakers are only reachable with it open
powergrid_modernized.ponder.tag.distribu: Panels, switchgear and bus duct: getting power from the service to every load behind its own breaker
powergrid_modernized.ponder.tag.radio.de: Dishes, sectors and omnis: Cat6 across the air, from point-to-point hops to a carrier network of towers
Boxes, conduit, pulled wire and the bender: raceway from a panel to every device, the way it is done on a job
powergrid_modernized.ponder.radio_dish_l: A radio is the indoor unit: a line and neutral at 50 W, a Cat6 jack for the computer network, a conduit knockout, and a coax port out to its antenna
Coax runs from the radio to the antenna, up to 64 blocks a span. Reach falls with the run, full to 16 blocks and half at 64, so keep it short and clip it to cable hangers up the mast
A dish on the coax makes the radio one end of a point-to-point link. Sneak-click the radio and type a link ID; both ends carry the same one
Aim each dish at the other to a tenth of a degree: sneak-click a dish for its azimuth and elevation, or clip the Alignment Scope on one and then the other and both are sighted in
Within reach and inside the 1° beam, the two radios' Cat6 jacks join as if a cable ran between them: one network, up to 2000 blocks apart. Goggles on a dish show how far off axis it is
powergrid_modernized.ponder.radio_carrie: A sector antenna is a base station: an aimed panel 30° to 180° wide, 120° by default, with a little downtilt. Its radio's link ID is the carrier, shared by every tower of that carrier
The beam is where it serves. Reach is 1000 blocks for a 120° sector and grows as the beam narrows: 2000 at 30°. Sneak-click any antenna with the Alignment Scope to draw its coverage in the world
An omni antenna is the client, 500 blocks of reach in all directions. Give its radio the carrier's ID and it joins the nearest sector whose beam covers it with a seat free, 16 to a sector
Omnis roam: on a vehicle or a Sable body they hand over to the next tower as they move, and the computers on both jacks stay one network the whole way
